newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia and UPM bolster holiday-hit Helsinki bourse.
newsitem.headline: Nokia and UPM bolster holiday-hit Helsinki bourse.

text.p: Shares closed holiday-dented trade higher, taking their cue from overnight gains in U.S. stocks, with firmer telecoms major Nokia and forestry group UPM-Kymmene in focus.
The Helsinki general index rose 0.82 percent to close at 2481.97 points.

Bourse engine Nokia rose at the opening to match its New York close and remained firm and stable for most of the session, ending up 3.90 markka at 265.90. Nokia's two share series accounted for 38 percent of total bourse turnover.
The session's second most traded share UPM-Kymmene closed 0.50 markka higher at 95.00 after fair 34 million markka trade.
Pharmaceuticals group Orion was fairly lively after a press report that French investment bank Paribas had a buy recommendation on the share.
Its more liquid B share hit a new year-high of 176.00 markka before closing at 174.00, up 8.00, and Orion A rose 6.50 to a new year-high of 180.00 markka.

"The news gave a boost to the share," one broker said but added that Orion has been rising for some time already and that many international investment houses have tipped pharmaceuticals companies as risers next year.

Wholesale and retail group Kesko rose 0.90 markka to 64.90 after announcing an internal transaction to buy the Anttila chain from its Tuko unit which brokers said showed Kesko would try to keep Anttila even if may have to sell the rest of Tuko to comply with European competition rules.
